extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry / number theory working on IUT, Vojta-type inequalities, and Diophantine problems
extracted.subtask_description: A research-article level proof of Vojta-type diophantine inequalities for hyperbolic curves using techniques from Inter-Universal Teichmüller theory (IUT), theta-values loci, and detailed ramification/discriminant/conductor estimates. The paper develops local and global bounds (log-volume, discriminant, conductor, ramification divisors) and deduces consequences including abc and Szpiro over Q.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumptions of Theorem 6.1.1
rubrics_metrics.description: Many intermediate lemmas and propositions are stated 'Under the notations and assumptions of Theorem 6.1.1'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This encapsulates the global setup used throughout (choices of number fields L, L', Ltpd, modular/modified fields Lmod, existence of Initial Theta Data, choices of primes ℓ, normalization of arithmeticoids, and other hypotheses stated in Theorem 6.1.1). Many subsequent bounds and equivalences require these hypotheses to be in force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial Theta Data and arithmeticoid normalization
rubrics_metrics.description: The arguments require 'Initial Theta Data [Joshi, 2024c, § 2.4, § 3.1, § 3.3]' and the existence of chosen arithmeticoids y0 and y0' = ϕ(y0) with the 'same global normalization' for the number field they provide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This hypothesis is repeatedly invoked (notably in Theorem 6.10.1) and is essential for comparing Frobenius-shifted ('log-shifted') quantities, applying Joshi's fundamental estimate, and making global volume comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of prime ℓ (large prime technical conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Various estimates assume ℓ satisfies lower bounds (e.g., ℓ ≥ 5, ℓ ≥ 7) so that inequalities like log(ℓ)/ℓ ≥ 1/2 and small error term bounds hold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numerical simplifications and error bounds (terms like 20/ℓ, log(ℓ)/ℓ, 12/ℓ^2) rely on choosing ℓ sufficiently large (explicitly used: ℓ ≥ 5, ℓ ≥ 7). Many asymptotic simplifications replace small rational constants using these lower bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tamely ramified outside specified set and degree bound
rubrics_metrics.description: If L'/L is tamely ramified outside a specified finite set and [L' : L] ≤ ℓ^4 (by Lemma 6.3.2), then the wild ramification contribution at ℓ in the log-Different+log-Conductor estimate is bounded by log(ℓ)/4 (or similar explicit bounds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is used in Lemma 6.4.2 and elsewhere to control wild-ramification terms coming from Theorem 4.6.1 (log-Discriminant+log-Conductor Theorem). The explicit degree bound [L':L] ≤ ℓ^4 yields an explicit bound for the wild ramification term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unramifiedness at primes in Supp(qLtpd)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma 6.5.1: Suppose v ∈ Supp(qLtpd) and v does not divide 2,3,5,ℓ and v ∈ Vnon_Ltpd. Then L'/Ltpd is unramified over v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This assertion is cited from Mochizuki and follows from assumptions on primes in §4.1.2 and Mochizuki's Proposition 1.8; used to ignore contributions from such primes in ramification sums.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of Vdst_M (ramified primes of M)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma 6.6.1: For M with Lmod ⊆ M and M/Lmod Galois, v ∈ Vdst_M iff v divides 30ℓ or v ∈ Supp(qM + dM); equivalently the image of v in VLtpd is contained in Vdst_Ltpd. In particular Vdst_M is finite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives an explicit criterion to determine which primes contribute to the 'destination' ramification divisor Vdst_M; used to bound degrees and logs of ramification divisors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of Vdst_Q (ramified rational primes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma 6.7.1: For a rational prime vQ, vQ ∈ Vdst_Q iff vQ ramifies in L' iff vQ divides 30ℓ or vQ is in the image of Supp(qLtpd + dLtpd) (equivalently in image of Supp(qL + dL)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This characterizes which rational primes can ramify in L' and thus which p contribute nontrivially to global ramification/divisor sums. Important for splitting global volume/product into finitely many nontrivial local factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and normalization of ramification divisors s_{L*} and s^≤_{L*}
rubrics_metrics.description: Define s_{L*} = Σ_{v ∈ Vdst_{L*}} e_v · v, deg(s_{L*}) = Σ_v e_v · deg(v), and log(s_{L*}) = deg(s_{L*})/[L* : Q]; similarly for s^≤_{L*} using ι_v factors (depending on residue characteristic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These arithmetic divisors record ramification contribution in a normalized way and are used throughout to compare to discriminant and conductor terms; both the (absolute) degree and normalized log-degree are used in inequalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upper bound for log(s^≤) in terms of e*_mod and ℓ
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma 6.7.8 (paraphrase): Under hypotheses of Theorem 6.1.1 one has e*_{mod} · log(s^≤) ≤ (e*_{mod} · ℓ + ηprm) · (4/3) (up to the explicit constants given in the text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an explicit inequality bounding the normalized ramification divisor log(s^≤) by quantities depending on the modular exponent e*_{mod}, ℓ, and an error term ηprm; used to control terms appearing in volume bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local relation: log(s_{M,vQ})/p_v = log(p_v)/p_v (identity for local components)
rubrics_metrics.description: Equation (6.8.2): For an arithmetic divisor a_M and rational prime vQ, the local component satisfies log(s_{M,vQ})/p_v = log(p_v)/p_v (in the displayed derivation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This algebraic identity (derived from fi = n and standard local-degree relations) is used to relate local contributions of s to local residue characteristics and ultimately to discriminant/conductor local components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bound for components of s_{Lmod} away from small primes
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim (6.8.4)/(6.8.5): For p_vQ ∉ {2,3,5,ℓ}, log(s_{Lmod})_{vQ}/p_{vQ} ≤ (log(d_{Ltpd,vQ}) + log(f_{Ltpd,vQ}))/2 (equivalently log(s_{Lmod})_{vQ} ≤ (log(dLtpd,vQ) + log(fLtpd,vQ))*p_{vQ}/2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proved by applying Serre's lower bounds on differents and comparing ev to δ_v + fv, then summing to obtain normalized inequalities; used to dominate ramification divisors by discriminant+conductor contributions away from small exceptional primes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lower bound on differents => upper bound on inertia degrees
rubrics_metrics.description: Using Serre (Chap. III, Prop. 13): δ_v (the exponent of the different) satisfies ev − 1 ≤ δ_v (equivalently ev ≤ δ_v + 1), and with small-case handling leads to ev ≤ 2(δ_v + f_v) for primes not dividing 30ℓ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This technical inequality is used to pass from lower bounds on different exponents to upper bounds on ramification indices ev and thence to bounds on normalized ramification-degree contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global bound relating discriminant, ramification divisor, and modular data (Proposition 6.8.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposition 6.8.1: Under the notations and assumptions of Theorem 6.1.1 one has an explicit inequality of the form 1 + (log(dL') + log(s_Q))/(4ℓ) · ... ≤ (1 + (log(dLtpd) + log(fLtpd))/4 + error terms involving dmod/ℓ, log(ℓ), and small constants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This proposition gives a global comparison between discriminant/log(s_Q) of L' and the base invariants of Ltpd (discriminant + conductor), with explicit error terms; used to propagate local ramification bounds to the global setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimate linking log(s_Q) to log(dLtpd)+log(fLtpd)
rubrics_metrics.description: Equation (6.8.11): log(s_Q)/(2 dmod) ≤ (log(dLtpd) + log(fLtpd)) + log(2·3·5·...·ℓ) (with further simplifications to give bounds of the form (log(dLtpd)+log(fLtpd)) + 5 + log(ℓ) and then scaled by 4/ℓ to produce small error terms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This shows how the normalized ramification divisor over Q can be bounded in terms of discriminant+conductor of Ltpd plus explicit small prime contributions; used to absorb log(s_Q) terms into main global discriminant/conductor terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local ramification exponent upper bound (Lemma 6.10.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma 6.10.5: For primes u above p in various extensions one has log(e_u) ≤ 3 + 4 log(e*_{mod} · ℓ) (i.e., an explicit bound for local ramification exponents in terms of e*_{mod} and ℓ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derived from degree comparisons in tower of extensions and bounds like [L':L] ≤ ℓ^4 and group-size estimates; used in local volume computations for theta-values loci.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local log-volume upper bound at ramified rational prime (Proposition 6.10.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposition 6.10.9: For p = vQ ∈ Vdst_Q one has an explicit inequality bounding (1/ℓ*) · (− log Vol(ΘI_{Mochizuki,p})) by a linear combination of log(dL',vQ), −log(q_{vQ}), log(s_Q,vQ), and log(s^≤_{vQ}) with explicit coefficients involving ℓ and e*_{mod}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the key local estimate for primes that ramify in L' and supplies the contributions that sum to the global upper bound on log-volume; it is taken from Mochizuki's Step (v) and adapted in this paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zero contribution from inert/unramified primes (Proposition 6.10.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposition 6.10.10: For p = vQ ∈ Vnon_Q  ackslash Vdst_Q (i.e., rational primes not in destination set), one has (1/ℓ*) · (− log Vol(ΘI_{Mochizuki,p})) ≤ 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows that almost all rational primes (outside a finite set) give no positive contribution to the global upper bound; used to reduce the product/ sum over primes to a finite set of nontrivial terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archimedean contribution bound (Proposition 6.10.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposition 6.10.12: For the unique archimedean prime p = ∞ one has (1/ℓ*) · (− log Vol(ΘI_{Mochizuki,∞})) ≤ (ℓ + 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives a uniform bounded (and small, compared to main terms) contribution from the archimedean factor in the global log-volume sum; Mochizuki's Step (vii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Second Main Bound — global log-volume inequality (Theorem 6.10.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem 6.10.1: With the stated notation, initial theta-data and normalization assumptions, one has an inequality relating |log(q_{ϕ(y0),ℓ}) − log(q_{y0,ℓ})| ≤ (1/ℓ*) · log Vol(hull(ΘI_{Mochizuki})) + C_Θ · |log(q_{y0,ℓ})|, where C_Θ is given explicitly in terms of deg(dLtpd)+deg(fLtpd), dmod/ℓ, e*_{mod}·ℓ + ηprm, and log(q_ℓ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the global upper bound (the 'Second Main Bound' or log-volume bound) combining local estimates (Propositions 6.10.9–12) and Proposition 6.8.1. The constant C_Θ is computed and simplified using the ℓ-conditions and prior lemmas; the inequality is essential to compare Frobenius-shifted q-quantities with global volumes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of fundamental lower bound for log-volume (Joshi/Mochizuki Corollary 3.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proof crucially uses the fundamental estimate (Mochizuki, 2021c, Corollary 3.12) as established in Joshi, 2024c, Corollary 9.11.1.1 which provides a global lower bound for Vol(ΘI_{Mochizuki}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combining Joshi's lower bound with the global upper bound (Theorem 6.10.1 / (6.11.6)) yields contradictions / inequalities that force the desired arithmetic bounds. The compatibility of the normalization of arithmeticoids is important for comparing the lower and upper bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deduction of Vojta's inequality for hyperbolic curves (Theorem 7.1.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem 7.1.1: For a geometrically connected, smooth, projective curve X over number field L, reduced divisor D with UX = X − D hyperbolic, for d ∈ N and any ε > 0 one has h_{ω_X(D)} ≤ (1 + ε)(log-diff_X + log-con_D) on UX(Q̄)_{≤ d} (up to bounded exceptional set Exc).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof reduces to the case X = P^1 with D = {0,1,∞} satisfying a 2-adic j-invariant condition, uses elliptic curves C_λ satisfying Theorem 6.1.1 and the bounds developed above; enlarging a finite exceptional set Exc handles degenerate cases. This is the main Diophantine conclusion of the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arithmetic consequences: abc and Szpiro over Q (Theorem 7.2.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem 7.2.1: From Theorem 7.1.1 one obtains Theorem 2.10.1: the abc-conjecture and the arithmetic Szpiro conjecture over Q are true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This records the central global arithmetic consequences deduced from the Vojta inequality proved in Theorem 7.1.1 and hence from the preceding chain of local/global estimates and volume comparisons.
